target_customer: Developers and companies building voice agents and interactive characters, from consumer apps to support, tutoring and entertainment
problem: Voice agents lack a face. LemonSlice turns a single image into a real-time interactive video avatar that talks live.
business_model: Usage-based API and embeddable widget, plans from 8 USD per month with credits per call minute

founders.name: Lina Colucci
previous_startups: Co-founded a profitable ML company (unnamed) that made 10 million USD, per YC page
founders.background_notes: From the YC page bio. Originally from Brazil.

founders.name: Sidney Primas
education: MIT PhD program in ML for medical imaging, dropped out
previous_startups: Edge Analytics (ML consulting firm, 12 engineers, 3M USD per year revenue)

founders.name: Andrew Weitz
founders.background_notes: From the YC page bio: 10 plus years in AI/ML and synthetic media.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time, single-image avatar generation at about 20 fps on one GPU needs custom video generation model research and low latency serving; the founders hold PhDs in ML and medical imaging.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary models trained on costly compute are hard to copy, but well funded avatar vendors and open research narrow the lead.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No competitor dated near the batch was verified in sources. No acquisition or copying found by 2026.

market_need_then: At batch time the product was pre-rendered talking videos from a single image (Infinity AI, launched on Product Hunt April 2024). The real-time voice agent need grew later, so early demand evidence is thin.

branding.name_origin: Company blog says the name Lemon Slice references a lemon slice resembling a smile, linked to its focus on talking characters (via search summary of the rebrand post).
branding.domain_note: Moved from the Infinity AI name to lemonslice.com after the rebrand; purchase details not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, positions itself as building the emotional engine for AI

rebrands.why: Company blog post titled Infinity AI is now LemonSlice; reason not read in full

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launch of the day for Infinity AI on 2024-04-10; site cites coverage from the New York Times, Forbes, TechCrunch and Gizmodo (vendor claim).

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct, friendly name with press coverage and a notable customer claim, though the company changed names and the brand is young.

pivots.from: Infinity AI, pre-rendered talking video generation from a single image
pivots.to: LemonSlice, real-time interactive avatars for voice agents
pivots.why: Not stated in opened sources; the company now sells a face layer for voice agents

outcome_analysis: LemonSlice started as Infinity AI in YC W24, shipped a talking video product in April 2024, and after rebranding raised a 10.5 million USD seed in December 2025 from Matrix and YC to build real-time avatars for voice agents. A research-heavy team, a live product with a reported Microsoft customer claim and the voice agent boom explain the raise. Heavy compute cost and well funded avatar competitors remain risks.
notes: One aggregator lists a 6M USD seed and another a 5M seed in 2022; these conflict with the TechCrunch reported 10.5M and are not recorded. Competitor search returned no sources dated near the batch, so the list is empty. The Microsoft customer quote is from the company's own site and unverified. The rebrand date was not found.
